mainTopic: The yearly times of judgment, whose opinion the משנה follows, and the reasons behind the holiday offerings and the שופר
overview: The משנה teaches that the world is judged four times a year: grain on פסח, tree fruit on עצרת, every person on ראש השנה, and rain on סוכות. The גמרא shows that each crop is actually judged twice, and אביי draws a farming lesson from this. It then asks whose opinion the משנה follows, since it fits none of the four views in a ברייתא (רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, רבי נתן). רבא answers that it follows the school of רבי ישמעאל. רב חסדא finds the source for רבי יוסי's view that people are judged every day, and learns from it that a king is judged before his people. רב יוסף asks whose view our daily prayers for the sick follow, and the גמרא brings רבי יצחק: crying out helps even after the verdict. A ברייתא explains that each holiday's offering brings blessing to what is judged then, and why ראש השנה has מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות. רבי אבהו explains why the שופר is a ram's horn. רבי יצחק then asks why we blow while sitting, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The four times the world is judged
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the world is judged four times a year: grain on פסח, tree fruit on עצרת, all people on ראש השנה, and water on סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are four times a year when the world is judged. On פסח, it is judged about grain. On שבועות, about fruit that grows on trees. On ראש השנה, every person passes before הקב״ה one by one, like sheep, as the פסוק says: 'He who forms all their hearts, who understands all their deeds.' On סוכות, they are judged about water (rain).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets out the four yearly judgment days and says what is decided on each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each judgment matches its season. Grain ripens around פסח, tree fruit around שבועות, and the rainy season begins after סוכות. Only ראש השנה is about people themselves, and the פסוק shows that הקב״ה looks at each person on their own.

keyTerms.meaning: Times or seasons of the year
Like sheep passing one at a time

steps.whatToRemember: פסח: grain. שבועות: tree fruit. ראש השנה: people. סוכות: rain.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
At four times of the year the world is judged:
On Pesach, concerning the grain;
on Atzeret, concerning the fruit of the tree;
phrases.notes: עצרת is what the משנה calls שבועות.

phrases.english: on Rosh Hashanah, all who come into the world
pass before Him like sheep,
as it is said: "He who fashions their hearts together,
phrases.notes: תהלים 33:15

phrases.english: who understands all their deeds";
and on the Festival they are judged concerning the water.
phrases.notes: 'The Festival' means סוכות, and 'water' means the rain for the coming year.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four judgments each year: grain on פסח, tree fruit on עצרת, people on ראש השנה, water on סוכות.

steps.title: Which grain is judged on Pesach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which grain the משנה means. It rules out the grain already standing in the field, because the things that happened to it earlier would never have been judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which grain is judged on פסח? Suppose you say it is the grain already standing in the field. Then when was a decision made about everything that already happened to it while it was growing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'grain' in the משנה means. It tests one possible answer and shows that it doesn't work. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By פסח, the standing grain has already lived through a whole winter of good and bad events. If its judgment only came on פסח, those earlier events would have happened without any judgment. So the משנה cannot mean that grain.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
That is standing (already grown in the field)

phrases.english: GEMARA
Which grain?
If you say this grain that is standing in the field,
all those events that already passed over it
when were they judged?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the word 'grain' in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which grain the פסח judgment refers to.

steps.title: The grain about to be sown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means the grain that will be sown in the coming year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the grain that is going to be sown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the פסח judgment is about next year's crop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fixes the problem from step 2. The judgment comes before the crop is planted, so everything that happens to it while it grows is already covered.

keyTerms.meaning: That is going to be sown

phrases.english: Rather, it is the grain that will be sown.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסח judgment is about the coming year's grain.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows two judgments for one crop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this means each crop gets only one judgment. It quotes a ברייתא showing that the same crop is judged by two different פסח judgments.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean a crop is judged only once? But a ברייתא teaches: if grain has a mishap before פסח, it was decided at the previous judgment. If it happens after פסח, it was decided at this פסח for the future. In the same way, if a person has a mishap before יום הכפורים, it was decided at the past judgment. If it happens after יום הכפורים, it was decided for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 3, which seemed to say a crop is judged only once, before it is sown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain grows across פסח. The ברייתא says that what happens to it before פסח was decided at last year's פסח, and what happens after was decided at this פסח. So one crop is covered by two judgments, not one.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a mishap or chance event
For the past / for the future

steps.confusionAlert: Here קרי does not mean its usual halachic meaning. It simply means something that happened, a mishap.

phrases.english: Is this to say that only one judgment is passed?
But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: תְּבוּאָה שֶׁאֵירַע בָּהּ קֶרִי אוֹ אוֹנֶס,
phrases.english: Grain that suffered an incident or an accident:
before Pesach, it was judged in the past;
phrases.notes: Meaning at the previous year's פסח.

phrases.english: after Pesach, it was judged for the future.

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם שֶׁאֵירַע בּוֹ קֶרִי אוֹ אוֹנֶס,
phrases.english: A person who suffered an incident or an accident:
before Yom Kippur, he was judged in the past;
after Yom Kippur, he was judged for the future.

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea from step 3 that a crop is judged only once, before it is sown.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא splits one growing crop between two פסח judgments: before פסח and after פסח.

steps.title: רבא: there are two judgments
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts what the ברייתא shows: each crop is judged twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: we learn from this that two judgments are made.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not push back on the challenge. He accepts the ברייתא as proof that a crop gets two judgments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer from step 3 still stands: the פסח judgment covers the crop that will be sown. But that same crop is judged again at the next פסח for the rest of its growth. So the period before פסח and the period after פסח each have their own judgment.
steps.whatToRemember: A single crop is judged twice: once before it is sown, and again at the next פסח.

phrases.english: Rava said: Learn from this
that two judgments are passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תְּרֵי דִינֵי מִתַּדְנָא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each crop is judged twice, at two different פסח judgments.

steps.title: אביי's farming advice
steps.stepSummary: אביי builds on רבא: if the slow-ripening crops are doing well, quickly plant a fast-ripening crop. It will finish growing under this year's good judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: so, if a person sees that his late crops are doing well, he should hurry and plant an early crop. By the time it reaches its next judgment, it will already have grown.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a practical lesson from רבא's rule of two judgments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slow crops are succeeding, that shows this year's judgment was good. A fast crop planted now will ripen before the next פסח judgment. So it grows entirely under the current good judgment.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the rule of two judgments affects real decisions about planting.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חָזֵי אִינָשׁ דְּמַצְלַח זַרְעָא אַפְלָא —
phrases.english: when a person sees that the late-ripening crop is succeeding,
he should hurry and sow an early-ripening crop,
for by the time it reaches its judgment, it will already have come up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's two-judgment rule to farming practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When late crops are doing well, quickly plant early crops so they ripen under the current favorable judgment.

steps.title: Whose opinion is our משנה? It fits none of the four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא our משנה follows, and says it does not fit רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי or רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה? It is not רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה, not רבי יוסי, and not רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote our משנה and points out that it does not match any of the four known opinions. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next, which lays out those four opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the world is judged at four separate times: grain on פסח, fruit on עצרת, people on ראש השנה, and water on סוכות. The גמרא claims no known תנא holds exactly this. It is a real difficulty, not just a request for information.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Asks which תנא is the author of the משנה

phrases.english: Whose opinion is our Mishnah?
Not Rabbi Meir,
and not Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְלָא רַבִּי נָתָן.
phrases.english: and not Rabbi Yosei, and not Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about who wrote the משנה, moving on from אביי's practical advice.
steps.kashyaTarget: Who wrote the משנה's list of four judgment times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every known opinion about when judgment happens differs from the משנה's list, so the משנה seems to have no author.

steps.title: The opinions of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר puts all judgment on ראש השנה with sealing on יום הכיפורים. רבי יהודה says all are judged on ראש השנה but each is sealed at its own time.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: Everything is judged on ראש השנה, and the sentence is sealed on יום הכיפורים. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: Everything is judged on ראש השנה, and each sentence is sealed at its own time. Grain is sealed on פסח, tree fruit on עצרת, and on סוכות they are judged about water. A person is judged on ראש השנה, and his sentence is sealed on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its claim. This first part shows why the משנה does not match רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר has only one judgment day, so he clearly does not fit a משנה with four times. רבי יהודה does have four times, but for him the main judging of everything happens on ראש השנה, and the four times are only when each sentence is sealed. The משנה says the world is actually judged on פסח, עצרת and סוכות.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep two stages apart: being judged (נידון) and having the sentence sealed (נחתם). רבי יהודה puts the judging of everything on ראש השנה. Only the sealing is spread across the year.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
All are judged on Rosh HaShanah,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁלָּהֶם נֶחְתָּם בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: and their sentence is sealed on Yom Kippur,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל נִידּוֹנִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: All are judged on Rosh HaShanah,
and their sentence is sealed
each and every one in its own time:
on Pesach, concerning grain;
on Atzeret, concerning fruit of the tree;
phrases.notes: עצרת is the name the גמרא uses for שבועות.

phrases.english: on the Festival they are judged concerning water.
phrases.notes: "The Festival" means סוכות.

phrases.english: And a person is judged on Rosh HaShanah,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁלּוֹ נֶחְתָּם בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: and his sentence is sealed on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind step 7's claim, starting with רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the opinions of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה

steps.title: רבי יוסי and רבי נתן: judged every day or every hour
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי יוסי says a person is judged every day, and רבי נתן says every hour. Each brings a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A person is judged every day, as it says, "You visit him every morning." רבי נתן says: A person is judged every hour, as it says, "You test him every moment."
steps.whatsHappening: The rest of the ברייתא gives the last two opinions. It shows the משנה cannot be רבי יוסי or רבי נתן either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two תנאים do not tie judgment to set times of the year at all. For them, a person is judged constantly. That clashes with the משנה, which gives people one fixed day, ראש השנה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם נִידּוֹן בְּכׇל יוֹם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: A person is judged every day,
as it is stated: "You visit him every morning."
phrases.notes: איוב 7:18

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אָדָם נִידּוֹן בְּכׇל שָׁעָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: A person is judged every hour,
as it is stated: "You test him every moment."
phrases.notes: איוב 7:18, the second half of the same פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם נִידּוֹן בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 8 with the last two opinions.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי or רבי נתן

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is רבי יהודה, talking about sealing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה really follows רבי יהודה, and that its four times refer to when each sentence is sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: Really, the משנה is רבי יהודה, and when the משנה lists its times, it is talking about the sealing of the sentence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a possible answer: the משנה follows רבי יהודה after all. This is a suggestion that the גמרא is about to test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already has grain on פסח, fruit on עצרת and water on סוכות, the same times as the משנה. The only difference is that he calls them sealing times, not judging times. So the suggestion is to read the משנה's word "judged" as meaning "sealed."

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. Brings up a possible answer, usually to reject it

phrases.english: And if you will say:
Really, it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and when our Mishnah teaches its times,
it is about the sentence being sealed,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's "judged" should be read as "sealed," since for רבי יהודה the actual judging is all on ראש השנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way out of step 7's difficulty, based on רבי יהודה's view in step 8.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is רבי יהודה and is listing sealing times.

steps.title: That fails: people are a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. If the משנה lists sealing times, it should put people on יום הכיפורים, not ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there is a difficulty from people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 10. The next step gives a new answer to who wrote the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a person's sentence is sealed on יום הכיפורים. If the משנה were listing sealing times, it should have said people are sealed on יום הכיפורים. Instead it puts people on ראש השנה, so the reading does not work.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not fit any of the four תנאים. Reading it as רבי יהודה's sealing times fails because the משנה puts people on ראש השנה, while רבי יהודה seals people's sentence on יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: If so,
there is a difficulty with people!
phrases.notes: The משנה puts people on ראש השנה, but for רבי יהודה a person's sentence is sealed on יום הכיפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer offered in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the משנה follows רבי יהודה by listing sealing times
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For people, רבי יהודה's sealing day is יום הכיפורים, but the משנה says ראש השנה.

steps.title: רבא: The משנה Follows the School of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא says our משנה matches a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל, which lists four times of judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Our משנה follows a teacher from the school of רבי ישמעאל. That school taught: The world is judged at four times. On פסח it is judged about grain. On עצרת it is judged about tree fruit. On סוכות it is judged about water. A person is judged on ראש השנה, and his sentence is sealed on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: After four תנאים failed to fit our משנה, רבא finds a fifth source that matches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא lists the same four times as our משנה: grain, fruit, water, and people. It also adds that a person's sentence is sealed on יום הכיפורים, a detail our משנה does not mention.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא,
phrases.english: This is a tanna from the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
At four times the world is judged:
On Pesach, about the grain;
on Atzeres, about the fruits of the tree;
on the Chag, they are judged about the water.
phrases.notes: "The Chag" means סוכות.

phrases.english: And a person is judged on Rosh Hashanah,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁלּוֹ נֶחְתָּם בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: and his sentence is sealed on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 11 rejected the רבי יהודה answer, רבא gives a new answer to the question from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a different תנא whose view matches the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to fit none of the known תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the school of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: The משנה Only Mentions the Start of Judgment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says people are judged on ראש השנה because that is when judgment begins. The sealing on יום הכיפורים is simply not mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: When our משנה teaches that people are judged on ראש השנה, it is talking about the beginning of the judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why our משנה leaves out יום הכיפורים, even though the ברייתא mentions it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For people, the ברייתא describes two stages: judgment on ראש השנה and sealing on יום הכיפורים. Our משנה names only the first stage. This also answers the problem from step 11, because the משנה was never listing sealing times.

keyTerms.meaning: About the beginning of the judgment

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows the school of רבי ישמעאל. For people, it names the start of judgment, ראש השנה, and not the sealing on יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: And when our Mishnah teaches,
it is about the beginning of the judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's answer by fitting the משנה's wording to the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה as describing only one stage of the process
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the ברייתא mentions יום הכיפורים, it might seem the משנה should mention it too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only when judgment begins.

steps.title: רב חסדא Asks for רבי יוסי's Reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks what the source is for רבי יוסי's view that a person is judged every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is the reason for רבי יוסי's view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוסי's view from step 9 and asks what his source is. This sets up the next few moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said a person is judged every day. רב חסדא is asking what supports that view.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about רבי יוסי's view from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יוסי's view

steps.title: But רבי יוסי Already Gave His Verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question, since רבי יוסי already quoted a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why ask? He already stated his reason: 'You visit him every morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's question, because the ברייתא already gives רבי יוסי's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רבי יוסי brought the פסוק 'You visit him every morning.' So it seems there is nothing left to ask.

phrases.english: As he stated his reason:
"You visit him every morning"!
phrases.notes: איוב 7:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the question asked in step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's source is already written in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The Real Question: Why Not Follow רבי נתן?
steps.stepSummary: The question really is why רבי יוסי did not hold like רבי נתן. One possible reason is that 'trying' means only looking, not judging.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we mean: why did רבי יוסי not hold like רבי נתן? You might say that 'trying' is only looking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב חסדא was really asking. It also suggests a reason that will be tested in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק goes on to say 'You try him every moment,' which is רבי נתן's source. If רבי יוסי accepts the first half of the פסוק, why not the second? A possible answer is that 'trying' is only examining, not real judgment.

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי נָתָן?
phrases.english: What is the reason he did not hold like Rabbi Nasan?
"Trying" is merely examining.
phrases.notes: This is about רבי נתן's words in the same פסוק, "You try him every moment."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by restating the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining what the question was really asking
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא seemed to be asking for a source that was already known.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking why רבי יוסי did not accept רבי נתן's half of the פסוק.

steps.title: Visiting Is Also Just Looking
steps.stepSummary: If 'trying' is just looking, then 'visiting' is also just looking. So רבי יוסי's פסוק does not prove judgment either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'visiting' not also just looking?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reason from step 16, because the same logic would also weaken רבי יוסי's own word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'trying' is not judgment, then 'visiting' is not judgment either. So the first פסוק cannot be a good source for רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: "Visiting" is also merely examining!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion from step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of 'You visit him every morning' as רבי יוסי's source
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Visiting' and 'trying' are both just examining, so neither one proves judgment.

steps.title: A Better Verse for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings a new פסוק that speaks about judgment 'each day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: רבי יוסי's reason comes from here: 'To do the judgment of His servant and the judgment of His people Israel, each day as it needs.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first פסוק did not work, רב חסדא brings a different one for רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק uses the word 'judgment' itself, so it cannot be read as just looking. It also says 'each day,' which matches רבי יוסי's view.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's real source is 'דבר יום ביומו,' which clearly speaks about daily judgment.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
The reason of Rabbi Yosei is from here:
"To do the judgment of His servant
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:59

phrases.english: and the judgment of His people Israel,
each day as it needs."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source that was rejected in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's source was 'You visit him every morning.'

steps.title: A King Is Judged Before the Community
steps.stepSummary: From the same פסוק, רב חסדא learns that a king is judged before his people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא also said: When a king and a community are judged, the king goes in first, since it says 'the judgment of His servant' and only then 'the judgment of His people Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא learns a new law from the order of words in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His servant' means the king, and he is mentioned before 'His people Israel.' The order in the פסוק teaches the order of judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes in first to be judged

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
A king and a community:
the king enters first for judgment,
as it says: "To do the judgment of His servant
phrases.notes: "His servant" is the king, שלמה, who said this prayer.

phrases.english: and the judgment of His people Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק from step 18 to teach a new rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king is judged before the community.

steps.title: Why Does the King Go First?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind this order.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the king is judged first. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows the order, but it does not explain why. The גמרא wants the reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the king is judged first

steps.title: Two Reasons the King Is Judged First
steps.stepSummary: First reason: it is not respectful to keep a king waiting outside. Second reason: he is judged before God's anger grows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: it is not proper for a king to sit outside and wait. Or if you want, say: he goes in before God's anger grows stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two possible reasons why the king is judged first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is about the king's honor. The second is about protecting him. If he were judged after the people, their sins could make the judgment harsher, so he goes in before the anger builds.
steps.whatToRemember: A king is judged first, either out of respect for him or to protect him before God's anger grows.

phrases.english: If you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְמֵיתַב מַלְכָּא אַבָּרַאי.
phrases.english: It is not proper manners for the king to sit outside.
And if you want, say:
It is before the burning anger grows.
phrases.notes: Anger at the people's sins could make his judgment harsher, so he goes in first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְמֵיתַב מַלְכָּא אַבָּרַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two reasons: the king's honor, or being judged before God's anger grows.

steps.title: Whose opinion do our daily prayers for the sick follow?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks which opinion lets us pray every day for the sick and suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Whose opinion are we following nowadays when we pray every day for the sick and those in pain?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks a practical question about our everyday prayers. He is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say a person is judged only once a year, on ראש השנה. If the judgment is already sealed, why pray for the sick on an ordinary day? So רב יוסף asks which view makes our daily prayer make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The sick and those in pain

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
In accordance with whom do we pray nowadays
for the sick and the suffering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the earlier argument about when a person is judged to real daily prayer practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion about the timing of judgment supports praying daily for the sick.

steps.title: First answer: like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Our daily prayers follow רבי יוסי, who says a person is judged every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion? Like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers his own question: we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person is judged every day, then every day there is a new judgment to pray about. That makes daily prayer for the sick fit perfectly.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי is the one from the earlier steps who says people are judged every single day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Daily prayer follows רבי יוסי, since each day brings a new judgment.

steps.title: Second answer: even like the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Another option: our prayers can follow even the רבנן, together with רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really it follows the רבנן, together with what רבי יצחק says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer so that our practice does not have to depend only on רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if judgment happens only once a year, prayer could still help later. The proof for that idea comes in the next step from רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (another answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually, it is in accordance with the Rabbis,
and in accordance with Rabbi Yitzchak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second possible answer to the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Daily prayer fits even the רבנן, if we add רבי יצחק's idea that prayer helps after judgment too.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: crying out helps before and after the verdict
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that crying out to God helps even after the judgment is decided.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said: Crying out to God is good for a person both before the verdict and after the verdict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יצחק to back up the second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the verdict was set on ראש השנה, prayer can still change it afterward. So praying daily for the sick makes sense even according to the רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Our daily prayers for the sick fit either רבי יוסי (judged daily) or the רבנן plus רבי יצחק (prayer helps even after the verdict).

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Crying out is good for a person
both before the verdict
and after the verdict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the second answer.
steps.raayaObject: That prayer has value even according to the רבנן's once-a-year judgment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק's statement that crying out helps before and after the verdict.

steps.title: Why the עומר is brought on פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that the עומר is brought on פסח so the grain in the fields will be blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה said in the name of רבי עקיבא: Why did the תורה say to bring the עומר on פסח? Because פסח is the time of grain. ה׳ said: Bring the עומר before Me on פסח, so the grain in the fields will be blessed for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא explaining the reasons behind the holiday offerings. First up: the עומר on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח is the season of grain, when the grain harvest begins, and the משנה said grain is judged then. Bringing a grain offering at that time asks ה׳ to bless the grain crop.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on פסח

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
Why did the Torah say
bring the omer on Pesach?
Because Pesach is the time of grain,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Bring the omer before Me on Pesach,
so that the grain in the fields will be blessed for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה הָבִיאוּ עוֹמֶר בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא about the purpose of the holiday offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עומר on פסח brings blessing to the grain.

steps.title: Why the שתי הלחם are brought on עצרת
steps.stepSummary: The two loaves on שבועות bring blessing to the fruit of the trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did the תורה say to bring the two loaves on עצרת? Because עצרת is the time of the fruit of the trees. ה׳ said: Bring the two loaves before Me on עצרת, so the fruit of the trees will be blessed for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the second holiday: the two loaves on שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same pattern as the עומר: the offering is brought at the time of judgment for a crop. Here the crop is tree fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves offered on שבועות

phrases.english: And why did the Torah say
bring the two loaves on Atzeret?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעֲצֶרֶת זְמַן פֵּירוֹת הָאִילָן הוּא,
phrases.english: Because Atzeret is the time of the fruit of the tree,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Bring the two loaves before Me on Atzeret,
so that the fruit of the tree will be blessed for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה הָבִיאוּ שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם בָּעֲצֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the same list of reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם on עצרת bring blessing to tree fruit.

steps.title: Why water is poured on סוכות
steps.stepSummary: Pouring water on the altar on סוכות brings blessing to the year's rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did the תורה say to pour water on the חג? ה׳ said: Pour water before Me on the חג, so the rains of the year will be blessed for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the third holiday, סוכות, and the water pouring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוכות is when the world is judged about water. Pouring water on the altar asks for a blessed rainy season.

keyTerms.meaning: Pouring water on the altar on סוכות

phrases.english: And why did the Torah say
pour water on the festival?
phrases.notes: "The festival" here means סוכות, when water was poured on the מזבח.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Pour water before Me on the festival,
so that the rains of the year will be blessed for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה נַסְּכוּ מַיִם בֶּחָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water pouring on סוכות brings blessing to the rains.

steps.title: Why we say מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: On ראש השנה we crown ה׳ as King, ask to be remembered for good, and do it through the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say before Me on ראש השנה מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות. מלכיות, so you will make Me King over you. זכרונות, so your remembrance will come before Me for good. And with what? With the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with ראש השנה and explains the three special sections of the מוסף prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the other holidays, ראש השנה is not about a crop but about accepting ה׳ as King and being remembered well. The שופר is the tool that carries this remembrance up before ה׳.
steps.whatToRemember: Each holiday's מצוה matches what is being judged then: grain on פסח, tree fruit on שבועות, rain on סוכות, and on ראש השנה we accept ה׳ as King and are remembered through the שופר.

phrases.english: And say before Me on Rosh HaShanah
Kingships, Remembrances, and Shofarot.
Kingships, so that you will make Me King over you;

phrases.aramaic: זִכְרוֹנוֹת — כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה זִכְרוֹנְיכֶם לְפָנַי לְטוֹבָה,
phrases.english: Remembrances, so that your remembrance will rise before Me for good;
and with what? With the shofar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִמְרוּ לְפָנַי בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מַלְכִיּוֹת זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item of the ברייתא's list, now about ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלכיות to crown ה׳‎, זכרונות to be remembered for good, through the שופר.

steps.title: Why use a ram's horn?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks why the שופר is made from a ram's horn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Why do we blow with a שופר of a ram?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the שופר just mentioned, רבי אבהו asks why it should be a ram's horn. He is setting up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the שופר carries our remembrance. Now רבי אבהו asks what is special about a ram in particular.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Why do we blow with a shofar of a ram?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the mention of the שופר at the end of step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the שופר is specifically a ram's horn.

steps.title: The ram's horn recalls עקידת יצחק
steps.stepSummary: A ram's horn reminds ה׳ of the ram offered in place of יצחק, and counts as if we bound ourselves before Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said: Blow before Me with a שופר of a ram, so that I will remember for you the binding of יצחק son of אברהם, and I will count it for you as if you had bound yourselves before Me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers: the ram's horn reminds ה׳ of עקידת יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the עקידה a ram was offered instead of יצחק. Blowing a ram's horn brings that merit back to mind, and ה׳ treats it as if we ourselves showed the same total devotion.

keyTerms.meaning: The binding of יצחק on the altar
I will count it for you

steps.whatToRemember: We use a ram's horn to bring up the merit of עקידת יצחק, and ה׳ counts it as if we bound ourselves.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for why a ram's horn is the preferred שופר on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Blow before Me with a shofar of a ram,
so that I will remember for you
the binding of Yitzchak son of Avraham,
and I will consider it for you
as if you had bound yourselves before Me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבהו's question from step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ram's horn recalls עקידת יצחק and counts as if we bound ourselves before ה׳.

steps.title: Why do we blow the שופר on ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק asks why we blow the שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Why do we blow the שופר on ראש השנה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement of רבי יצחק opens with a question: why do we blow the שופר on ראש השנה? This opening question sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the question seems to ask for the reason behind the מצוה of שופר itself. The next lines show that this simple reading can't be what רבי יצחק meant.

keyTerms.meaning: we blow (the שופר); from תְּקִיעָה, a long straight blast
the New Year, the day of שופר

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Why do we blow the shofar on Rosh Hashanah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לָמָּה תּוֹקְעִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching of רבי יצחק about the שופר. It follows the earlier discussion of why the שופר is a ram's horn.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for blowing the שופר on ראש השנה.

steps.title: The Torah openly commands blowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: how can you ask why we blow, when the תורה says 'blow'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do we blow?! The Merciful One said, 'Blow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יצחק's question. Why ask for a reason to blow, when the פסוק plainly commands it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clear command from the תורה needs no reason to explain why we do it. So the simple reading of רבי יצחק's question cannot be right. He must have meant something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the Merciful One', meaning ה׳, the Giver of the תורה

phrases.english: Why do we blow?!
The Merciful One said, "Blow!"
phrases.notes: תהלים 81:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain reading of the question in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question 'why do we blow' in step 32.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק openly commands blowing, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: Maybe the question is about the תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the question: maybe he asked why we blow a תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is: why do we blow a תרועה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new reading of רבי יצחק's question. Maybe he was asking only about the תרועה, the broken, sobbing sound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק quoted only said 'blow', which matches a תקיעה. So the גמרא suggests the question was about the extra sound, the תרועה. This new reading is about to be tested too.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; it introduces a new reading
we blow a תְּרוּעָה (broken, staccato blasts)

phrases.english: Rather: why do we blow a teruah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33 by rereading the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading what the question was really asking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about blowing the שופר in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was about the תרועה in particular.

steps.title: The Torah openly commands the תרועה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again: the תורה says 'זכרון תרועה', so the תרועה is commanded as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do we blow a תרועה?! The Merciful One said, 'a remembrance of תרועה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second reading the same way it rejected the first. The תרועה is also written openly in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about ראש השנה names the day 'זכרון תרועה'. So the תרועה is also a clear command and needs no reason. The question still has not been found.

keyTerms.meaning: 'a remembrance of תרועה', the תורה's name for ראש השנה

phrases.english: Blow a teruah?!
The Merciful One said, "a remembrance of teruah"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new reading offered in step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי יצחק asked why we blow a תרועה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק openly commands the תרועה, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The real question: blowing while sitting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on the real question: why do we blow תקיעות and תרועות while the people are sitting?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is: why do we blow תקיעות and תרועות while the people are sitting,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally reaches what רבי יצחק really asked. He was asking about the custom of blowing while everyone is sitting. The sentence is not finished here and keeps going in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה commands תקיעה and תרועה, but it never says to blow at a time when the people are sitting. That practice is what needs a reason. The question now points at the order of the blowings, not the מצוה itself.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יצחק doubts the מצוה of שופר. The גמרא has just shown that blowing and the תרועה are both clear commands. The only question is about the custom of blowing while sitting.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the basis for the two sets of blowings on ראש השנה, one while sitting and another later.
